ja: 私、この会社で働いて5年になります。
en: I've been with this company for five years.
alternatives: I've worked at this company for five years.
I've been working here for five years.
point: 「5年になる」は現在完了。for + 期間で継続を表す

ja: 彼女、日本語と韓国語が話せるよ。
en: She can speak Japanese and Korean.
alternatives: She speaks Japanese and Korean.
She speaks both Japanese and Korean.
point: 「話せる」は can speak で言う

ja: 同じ神戸出身だと知っていたら、声をかけたのに。
en: If I'd known you're from Kobe too, I'd have said hi.
alternatives: If I'd known we're both from Kobe, I'd have said hello.
If I'd realized you're from Kobe too, I'd have spoken up.
point: 過去の事実の反対は If + had + 過去分詞、主節は would have

ja: 人違いかもしれませんが、前にお会いしましたよね？
en: I could be wrong, but haven't we met before?
alternatives: Sorry if I'm wrong, but haven't we met before?
I may be mistaken, but I think we've met before.
point: I could be wrong, but で断定を避ける

ja: 犬の散歩中は、いつも音楽を聴いてます。
en: I always listen to music while walking my dog.
alternatives: I listen to music whenever I walk my dog.
While walking my dog, I always listen to music.
point: 「〜しながら」は while + -ing で、主語は省ける

ja: 地元に恩返ししたくて、この仕事を選びました。
en: I chose this job to give back to my hometown.
alternatives: I took this job to give back to my hometown.
I chose this job because I wanted to give back.
point: 「恩返しする」は give back。目的は to 不定詞で言える

ja: こんにちは。私は看護師です。
en: Hello, I'm a nurse.
alternatives: Hi, I'm a nurse.
Hi. I work as a nurse.
point: 職業には a をつけて a nurse と言う

ja: もう英語で働くのに慣れた？
en: Are you used to working in English yet?
alternatives: Have you gotten used to working in English?
Have you gotten used to English at work?
point: be used to の後は動詞の ing 形

ja: あそこに立っている女性が私の上司です。
en: The woman standing there is my boss.
alternatives: The woman who's standing there is my boss.
That woman over there is my boss.
point: 「立っている女性」は the woman standing と後ろから説明する

ja: ケンが紹介してくれなかったら、会えなかったね。
en: If Ken hadn't introduced us, we'd never have met.
alternatives: We'd never have met if Ken hadn't introduced us.
Without Ken introducing us, we'd never have met.
point: 過去の仮定は had + 過去分詞、結果は would have met

ja: 祖父にちなんで名付けられたんです。
en: I was named after my grandfather.
alternatives: I was named for my grandfather.
I got my name from my grandfather.
point: 「名付けられた」は受動態。名前は after で由来を示す

ja: 自己紹介しないとね。僕はトムです。
en: I should introduce myself. I'm Tom.
alternatives: I have to introduce myself. I'm Tom.
I need to introduce myself. I'm Tom.
point: 「自己紹介する」は introduce myself、myself を忘れない

ja: 私の仕事は、ひと言では説明しにくいんです。
en: What I do is hard to sum up in one word.
alternatives: My job is hard to sum up in one word.
It's hard to sum up what I do in a word.
point: 「私の仕事」は What I do。what 節が主語になる

ja: ヨガを始めて、すっかりはまりました。
en: I took up yoga and got hooked.
alternatives: I started yoga and got really into it.
I started doing yoga and got hooked.
point: 「始める」は句動詞 take up、「はまる」は get hooked

ja: 僕が社交的だったらな。初対面だと固まっちゃう。
en: I wish I were outgoing. I freeze up around strangers.
alternatives: I wish I were sociable. I freeze up around strangers.
If only I were outgoing. I clam up around strangers.
point: 現在の願望は wish + 過去形、be動詞は were

ja: 僕の仕事は、アプリを設計することです。
en: What I do is design apps.
alternatives: I design apps for a living.
My job is designing apps.
point: What I do is の後は動詞の原形でも言える

ja: 不躾ですが、どんなお仕事をされているんですか？
en: Forgive my asking, but what do you do?
alternatives: Pardon my asking, but what do you do for work?
Sorry to be blunt, but what do you do?
point: Forgive my asking, but で質問を和らげる

ja: もし選べたら、あなたはどこに住みたい？
en: Where would you live if you could?
alternatives: If you could choose, where would you live?
If you could pick, where would you live?
point: if 節は過去形、主節は would + 原形

ja: 妻と出会っていなければ、今ここにはいないよ。
en: If I'd never met my wife, I wouldn't be here.
alternatives: If I hadn't met my wife, I wouldn't be here.
I wouldn't be here if I hadn't met my wife.
point: 過去の仮定は過去完了、今の結果は wouldn't be

ja: 昨年転職して、今は広告の仕事をしています。
en: I switched careers last year. Now I'm in advertising.
alternatives: I changed careers last year; now I'm in advertising.
I changed jobs last year; I'm in advertising now.
point: 昨年は過去形、今の状態は現在形で切り分ける

ja: 同業だったなんて、今まで気づきませんでした。
en: I hadn't realized we were in the same field.
alternatives: I didn't realize we worked in the same field.
I had no idea we shared a field.
point: 気づく前から同業だった。その差を過去完了で出す

ja: 何がきっかけで、ここに引っ越してきたんですか？
en: What was it that made you move here?
alternatives: What made you decide to move here?
What was it that made you move to this city?
point: What was it that で「何が」を強調する

ja: 来月、新しい仕事を始めるんです。
en: I'm starting a new job next month.
alternatives: I start a new job next month.
My new job starts next month.
point: 決まっている予定は現在進行形で言える

ja: この仕事の前は何をされてたか、伺えますか？
en: May I ask what you did before this?
alternatives: Could I ask what you did before this?
Can I ask what you did before this?
point: ask の後は what you did の語順、what did you do にしない

ja: お仕事は何をされているんですか？
en: What do you do for a living?
alternatives: What kind of work do you do?
What line of work are you in?
point: 職業は What do you do? で聞く。do が二回続く

ja: 上司に挨拶してこいと言われたんです。
en: My boss told me to say hello.
alternatives: My boss told me to say hi.
My boss told me to greet you.
point: 「〜するように言われた」は told me to do で言える

ja: 今日来ていなければ、あなたとは会えていませんでしたね。
en: Had I not come today, we'd never have met.
alternatives: If I hadn't come today, we'd never have met.
If I hadn't come today, I'd never have met you.
point: Had I not〜 は If I hadn't〜 の倒置形

ja: 田中さんから、あなたは大阪出身だと聞きました。
en: Tanaka told me you were from Osaka.
alternatives: Tanaka mentioned you were from Osaka.
I heard from Tanaka that you're from Osaka.
point: told の後の節は時制の一致で過去形にしやすい

ja: 私の家族は4人です。
en: There are four in my family.
alternatives: My family has four people.
We're a family of four.
There are four of us.
point: 「〜人いる」は There are 〜 で言う

ja: 前にどこかでお会いしているはずです。
en: We must have met somewhere before.
alternatives: I'm sure we've met somewhere before.
I'm pretty sure we've met somewhere before.
point: 過去への確信は must have + 過去分詞
